title: Outer-pixel subtraction removes the 12.426-day template signal within fit errors in two Kepler quarters of KOI-3967
abstract: We tested the pixels of KIC 5385697 in Kepler quarters 5 and 13. A waveform from nearby KIC 5385778 gives broad positive coefficients across each 20-pixel stamp after a fit for time trends and pointing. Subtraction of the mean flux outside the optimal aperture changes its fitted coefficient from 0.596 to -0.080 electron/s in Q5 and from 1.349 to 0.096 electron/s in Q13. Both residual block intervals include zero. Adding back the recorded background estimate leaves the waveform present. This supports a broad contaminating component under the tested model. It does not locate the source or distinguish optical light from electronic or calibration effects. The two quarters use one telescope. The selected template, short residual blocks, small stamps, and outer stellar light limit the test. We include all four input files, exact source URLs and hashes, code, sensitivity fits, figures, and reproduction instructions. No new planet is established.
